title: Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement
summary: replace New Tag and New Alias dependencies on bulk imports, then remove the obsolete registry and alias import capabilities without changing canonical tag data
content_html:
Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement

Result

/studio/tag-registry/ and /studio/tag-aliases/ maintain individual canonical tags and aliases without bulk vocabulary-import capabilities.

New Tag and New Alias use first-class create operations. Their import uploads, add/merge/replace modes, APIs, configuration, and executable implementations are removed after both create paths are proven.

Why

Bulk import was useful when establishing the current registry and aliases. It is now a high-blast-radius way to replace canonical vocabulary and can silently discard new fields as those records evolve.

Retiring both vocabulary imports also gives the downstream Flat Tag Identity migration one ordinary create/edit contract rather than import-specific merge and replacement semantics. Tag-document linking follows that identity migration.

Boundary

  • Preserve the current canonical tag IDs, registry records, and alias records; this feature has no data migration.
  • Preserve New Tag, New Alias, edit, delete, promotion/demotion, direct local writes, activity evidence, atomic replacement, and the supported manual patch fallback.
  • Remove the tag-registry and tag-alias import routes rather than retaining redirects, aliases, proxies, or compatibility adapters.
  • Offline assignment-session retirement is owned separately by Offline Tag Assignment Session Retirement.
  • Do not remove catalogue workbook import or unrelated import infrastructure.
  • Do not implement tag-document association or change the tag registry schema.

Delivery Order

  1. First-class Tag Creation Delivery removes the New Tag workflow's dependency on registry import.
  2. First-class Alias Creation Delivery removes the New Alias workflow's dependency on alias import.
  3. Bulk Tag Vocabulary Import Removal Delivery removes both now-unneeded bulk capabilities and their executable surfaces.

The removal delivery depends on both create deliveries. Each remains proposed until explicitly promoted through the Roadmap workflow.

Durable Destination

Shipped behavior belongs in Tag Registry and Tag Aliases. Tag Source Data receives only any lasting source-schema or write-boundary consequence.
